title: Pet-Friendly Villas in Koh Samui: Complete Guide for Travelling with Pets
description: Travelling to Koh Samui with your dog or cat? Here's how to find genuine pet-friendly villas, navigate Thai pet import rules, and keep your pet safe on the island.

blocks.text: Travelling with pets to Koh Samui requires more planning than a standard holiday, but it’s entirely possible and increasingly popular. Thailand’s island paradise is more pet-welcoming than many travellers expect — provided you do your homework on import regulations, villa policies, and on-island veterinary care. This guide covers everything you need before you travel with your furry companion.
Bringing a pet into Thailand requires documentation that must be arranged well in advance. The core requirements are:

items: ISO microchip — your pet must be microchipped with a 15-digit ISO 11784/11785 compliant chip.
Rabies vaccination — must be current and administered at least 21 days before travel.
Health certificate — issued by a licensed veterinarian within 10 days of departure and endorsed by your country’s official authority.
Import permit — apply to the Thai Department of Livestock Development at least 15 days before arrival.

blocks.text: Rules change — always verify the latest requirements with the Thai embassy in your country before travel.

The phrase “pet-friendly” in Koh Samui villa listings varies widely. Some properties accept small dogs under 5 kg only; others welcome all sizes. Some charge a cleaning deposit; others include it in the rate. Key questions to ask before booking:

items: Maximum pet size and number of pets allowed?
Is there a garden or outdoor area where pets can roam safely?
Are pets allowed inside the villa or only in outdoor areas?
Is there a pet deposit, and is it refundable?

blocks.text: The quieter northern beaches are best for travelling with dogs. Maenam Beach is long and largely uncrowded, particularly in the early mornings, and dogs on leashes are a common sight. The Fisherman’s Village in Bophut is dog-friendly by culture — many of the restaurants have outdoor seating where well-behaved dogs are tolerated.
Residential and calm, this area has wider roads with pavements in places and nearby Choeng Mon Beach is quieter than the main tourist beaches. Good for dogs that need space and regular walks.

Koh Samui has several veterinary clinics, with the most established being the Koh Samui Animal Hospital near Chaweng and the Samui Animal Clinic. Both offer general consultations, vaccinations, and emergency services. Bring a copy of your pet’s vaccination records and health certificate from home.
Keeping Your Pet Safe in a Tropical Climate

items: Heat — Thailand is hot year-round. Never leave pets in parked vehicles, limit walks to early morning and evening, and ensure freshwater is always available.
Insects and parasites — apply veterinarian-recommended flea, tick, and heartworm prevention before travel and maintain it throughout your stay.
Street dogs — Koh Samui has a significant stray dog population. Keep your pet on a leash and avoid areas where strays congregate to prevent confrontations.

Toxic plants — many tropical plants common in villa gardens (oleander, frangipani, sago palm) are toxic to dogs and cats. Check the villa garden and fence off accessible areas if your pet is a chewer.

blocks.text: Formally, dogs are not permitted on most Thai beaches. In practice, early morning walks on quieter beaches like Maenam, Bangrak, and Choeng Mon pass without issue if you keep your dog leashed and clean up after them. Avoid the main tourist beaches (Chaweng, Lamai) where enforcement is stricter.
Travelling Between Islands with Your Pet

If you plan day trips to Koh Phangan or Koh Tao, note that most ferry operators do not accept pets in passenger cabins. Some allow pets in carry cases in cargo — confirm directly with the ferry operator before booking. Flying within Thailand with a pet requires airline-specific advance booking (most carriers require pets to travel in the hold).
